extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of classical algebra (readers of a historical mathematical treatise)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted rules and definitions from a classical algebra treatise covering procedures for adding, subtracting, multiplying and reducing square and cube roots, and definitions/operations on binomials, medial lines, and rational/irrational quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additione radicum quadratarum cum cubia
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for adding square roots and cube roots (headed/phrased in the text as additione radicum quadratarum cum cubia / additio radicum cubicarum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the terms 'like' by multiplying/dividing so that magnitudes correspond (e.g., multiply factors so cubes and squares correspond to a common unit); when adding a cube to a square or vice versa, bring both to comparable powers (via multiplication by the smaller factor or by repeated fixed multiplications such as by 2, 8, 64, 4096 in examples) so they can be summed; examples use numeric illustrations (4096, 64, 128, etc.) showing reducing to the same nature before summation. The text emphasizes using 'regole ferme' (fixed rules) and reducing via the least (la minore) factor to align magnitudes before addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtractione radicum quadratarum et cubierum
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for subtracting square roots and cube roots (noted as subtractione radicum quadratarum et cubie).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same general approach as addition: convert terms to comparable units by multiplication/division so that one can remove (subtract) the smaller from the larger; keep track of the 'magione' (greater) and 'minore' (smaller) and operate by the fixed rule of bringing both to the same nature before subtraction. The passage gives prescriptions for when one root must be transformed or partitioned (partire la magione per la minore) prior to subtracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fumare / fotrare (sommare/multiplicare) radici mediante regole ferme
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of fixed multiplication rules (regole ferme) to transform roots before arithmetic (the text repeatedly instructs to 'moltiplica via la minore' or 'per regola ferma').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When confronting roots of different natures, repeatedly multiply by fixed factors (often powers of 2,8,64,4096 in examples) to produce terms of like nature; the smallest factor (la minore) is used as the basis for successive multiplications. The text shows algorithmic sequences (multiply, partition the greater by the lesser, repeat) and illustrates families of analogous operations for other cases. Also used when adding/subtracting/multiplying cubes and squares to produce 'una medefima natura' for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additio / subtractione tramite partizione e moltiplicazione
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding/subtracting a number to/from a root (or vice versa), partition the larger magnitude and multiply parts to align with the smaller before combining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: 'quando bauerai a cauare ... recarai lo numero a .^.cuba e bauerai alle mani co la cube' — i.e., bring the number into the form of the cube (or square) by multiplying/partitioning, then perform the operation termwise. The text gives procedural steps: transform, partition, multiply the remainder by the smaller factor, and then proceed; these steps repeat until terms are of same nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additione radicum cubicarum (addition of cubic roots)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific procedure for combining cubic roots among themselves by creating like units through multiplication and using 'regola ferma'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example-driven: multiply and combine cubes using powers and families of multiplications (e.g., cube multiples like 8, 64, 512, 4096) so that the cubes can be directly summed; the text prescribes producing 'famiglie' of similar terms and combining analogous members. Also shows how to generate analogous products by repeated multiplications 'via la minore' to create comparable terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: De mediali / linea mediale / superficie mediale (definition and properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and properties of 'linea mediale' (medial line) and 'superficies mediale' as used for non-square numbers and geometrical interpretation of irrationalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A medial line is described as a line whose square relates proportionally between non-square magnitudes (e.g., mediating between square and non-square quantities). The text explains how medial lines/surfaces arise in practical geometry and arithmetic: they are 'mezana fra due superfici' or 'mezana fra due numeri non quadrati', giving rise to medial proportions. It prescribes when lines are called medial, bimedial, etc., and how medial quantities compose and combine (e.g., bi-medial, tri-medial names and their properties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of rational and irrational quantities and naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of numbers/lines into rational (rationali) and irrational (irrationali) and systematic naming for compositions (primo, secondo, tertio, quarto binomio etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treatise distinguishes rational/directly commensurable quantities from irrational (incommensurable) ones, defines 'linea media' and different levels (bi-mediale, tri-mediale), and lists naming conventions for binomials and their successive powers and residues (primum, secundum, tertium, quartum, quintum, etc.). It explains how binomials composed of different terms are called and how their powers and residuals are treated in operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radici dei binomii (extracting roots of binomials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for finding roots of binomials and conditions under which a binomial has roots coinciding with those of another binomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section on 'radice primi binomi' states that many roots may coincide with those of the first binomial; it explains building a number from terms of different binomials by means of taking common roots and mediating terms. It prescribes an algorithmic approach: compare binomials, align terms (via the mediating of terms or matching of powers), and deduce roots; examples and numeric tests are given to illustrate the procedure and show how multiple binomials share root-structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and decomposition of binomials (naming, powers, and residues)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to compose binomials from terms, how to regard their powers (quadrata, cubo, potenzia) and how to derive residues/parts used in further algebraic operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that binomials are formed by two names (terms) and that other binomials and derived names (e.g., those arising from powers) have systematic relations. The text details how the power of a binomial is expressed in terms of the powers of its parts and the interplay of these in forming residues; it gives explicit rules for determining which parts correspond to which names when expanding powers and looking for residues. Numeric examples (squares and higher powers) illustrate how to allocate parts and how to multiply/divide to obtain desired forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic practice: use of numeric exemplars to illustrate general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the treatise, the author demonstrates rules with concrete numeric examples (4096, 64, 128, 729, 512, etc.) to show how to carry out the algebraic procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly transforms abstract rules into numeric sequences: multiply by given constants, partition magnitudes, and check that after successive operations terms reach the same 'natura' so they can be summed, subtracted, or have roots extracted. This exemplar-driven method is part of the prescriptive pedagogical approach: demonstrate the fixed rule once and then apply analogous multiplications for other similar cases (families of operations).
